decisions.title: Web hosting
decisions.body: Next.js is the web default. Vercel Pro runs it with every feature and no adapter. Cloudflare Workers (through the OpenNext adapter) is the best free host, and its free plan allows commercial use. Vercel's Hobby plan does not.

decisions.title: Getting paid
decisions.body: Selling software to customers in many countries: start with a merchant of record (Paddle), which collects and remits VAT and sales tax for you. Move to Stripe direct, with Stripe Tax, when you want lower fees and full control and can handle tax registrations yourself. Stripe is invite-only in some countries, including India; see the country notes.

decisions.title: Company formation
decisions.body: If you might raise venture money, the common default is a Delaware C-corp (Stripe Atlas or Clerky). Filing yourself is cheaper but not free: there is a state filing fee, a registered agent and annual franchise tax. If you won't raise, a local company in your own country is usually simpler. Country notes cover the UK, the EU and India.

decisions.title: Meeting notes
decisions.body: Granola for notes with no bot in the call, Fathom's free plan at zero budget. Health and other regulated data stay out of cloud note-takers unless the vendor signs the agreements you need.

decisions.title: One build workflow
decisions.body: The site's coding-agent stance is Claude Code. Use Superpowers for the plan, test and build loop, and Spec Kit only to write spec documents. Two planners in one repo give the agent conflicting instructions.

decisions.title: Jobs
decisions.body: A platform queue for fan-out and retries. A durable workflow engine (Inngest, or DBOS for free) for long, multi-step LLM jobs.

decisions.title: Newsletters
decisions.body: Your personal audience and your product's users are different lists: one tool each (see Personal brand and Sales + GTM).

decisions.title: Model APIs and customer data
decisions.body: Use a paid, no-training API tier for anything that touches customer data. Free tiers often allow human review or training on your inputs. Gemini's free tier also isn't allowed for apps serving users in the EU, Switzerland or the UK.

decisions.title: Healthcare clients
decisions.body: None of the free tiers in the default stack signs a HIPAA business associate agreement. AWS and Google Cloud let you accept one yourself; most SaaS vendors need a paid plan or a sales contract.

notes.title: Pin dependencies and actions
notes.body: LiteLLM had two separate supply-chain compromises in 2026: PyPI 1.82.7-1.82.8 in March, and v1.107.0 (PyPI and container images) on 21 October. Trivy's GitHub Action tags were hijacked in March. Pin packages and container digests, pin Actions to commit SHAs, and audit workflows with zizmor. If you installed an affected version, rotate every secret it could reach.

notes.title: Keep customer data off free AI tiers
notes.body: Free API tiers often allow training or human review, and some can't be used in the EU, Switzerland or the UK at all. Put customer and regulated data only on paid, no-training endpoints with the right agreements.

notes.title: Sandbox your coding agent
notes.body: Claude Code's Bash sandbox runs natively on macOS and Linux, and on Windows only inside WSL2. Prefer auto mode with allow and deny rules over skipping permission prompts, and open untrusted repositories inside a sandbox or dev container.

notes.title: Check licence terms at work
notes.body: Docker Desktop, OrbStack and some editors need a paid licence at companies above a size or revenue threshold, and some free tiers are personal-use only. Check before you standardise a team on them.

notes.title: Free tiers share quotas
notes.body: On most serverless free plans, every app in the account shares one request quota. Split noisy projects into separate accounts or move to the first paid tier when traffic grows.

phases.title: Set up your machine
steps: Install Claude Code; use auto mode with allow and deny rules instead of skipping permission prompts.
Set up your OS package manager (Homebrew on macOS, winget on Windows, your distro's on Linux) and a modern terminal.
Install the GitHub CLI and sign in: gh auth login.
Put secrets in a secrets manager, not in plaintext .env files.

phases.title: Claude Code core
steps: Add the official language-server plugins for your languages.
Choose one build workflow (Superpowers) and keep other planners out of the repo.
Add a browser tool for testing, a live-docs MCP and a web-search MCP.
Set a status line that shows usage limits and context.

phases.title: Accounts
steps: Create accounts for hosting, Postgres, auth, email, error tracking, analytics and uptime. Use the paid pick or the best free option from each Ship slot.
Register your domain and set up DNS and business email.
Get a production model API key on a no-training tier.

phases.title: Product stack
steps: Scaffold a TypeScript monorepo: Next.js, Hono, Drizzle on Postgres, Expo. Add Electron by hand if you need a desktop app.
Deploy the web app and API, and the MCP server if you have one.
Add tracing and evals in CI from day one.
Set up mobile builds and the app-store test tracks early; Play's closed-testing rule takes two weeks.

phases.title: Money and legal
steps: Form the company that fits your plans (see Decisions), open a business bank account and set up accounting.
Choose a merchant of record or Stripe, with tax handled.
Adopt standard contracts and e-signature, and publish a privacy policy that fits your users' countries.
Check your country's notes on tax registration and export invoicing with a professional.

phases.title: Sell
steps: Set up a CRM and prospecting data, and send from a separate warmed domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
Use one booking tool for interviews and sales calls, and a meeting-notes tool.
Ship a marketing site and docs with search consoles connected.
Add support, a feedback board and product demos when users arrive, then plan a launch.

phases.title: Run and grow
steps: Keep a notes system, a backlog and a calendar that protects focus time.
Post where your buyers are and keep a personal newsletter going.
Spend 45 minutes a week on the learning radar.

pick.name: Syften
pick.what: Multi-community monitor: Reddit, HN, Lobsters, forums, Slack communities, public web; API on all paid plans, MCP on PRO
pick.why: Widest coverage and filtering plus API/MCP; 14-day PRO trial, no card.
pick.free_limits: No free plan; 14-day PRO trial, no card. Entry $29.95/mo (3 community filters, 1 web filter, API), Standard $49.95 (20 filters, AI filtering, Slack), PRO $119.95 (100 filters, full archive, webhooks, MCP added 10 May 2026); X +$40/mo, YouTube +$20/mo add-ons

best_free.name: F5Bot
best_free.what: Free keyword email alerts for Reddit, Hacker News and Lobsters
best_free.why: The only credible $0 always-on listener now that GummySearch is gone. Pair it with Claude/Gemini Deep Research for one-off digs.
best_free.free_limits: Free forever: keyword alerts for Reddit, HN and Lobsters, email only, basic filtering (free keyword cap not stated). Terms: unpaid accounts licensed for internal use, personal or within your own organisation; no resale/redistribution of alerts. Silver $12.99/mo (20 keywords) is marketed 'for individuals, non-commercial use'; Gold $49.99/mo (200 keywords) 'for professionals and small businesses'

alts.name: Appfigures (free)
alts.what: App-store review mining for your own and competitor apps
alts.why: B2C/Android: competitor 1-2 star reviews are the cheapest problem list there is.
alts.free_limits: Free: 5 connected apps, review reports; no download/revenue estimates. Connect $9.99/mo

alts.name: HN Algolia search API
alts.what: Free full-text search over Hacker News
alts.why: Free ad hoc HN mining that scripts or an agent can query; not a monitor.

candidates.name: F5Bot
candidates.verdict: best_free: free keyword alerts for Reddit/HN/Lobsters; commercial terms of free plan unclear

slots.decision: Syften monitors the widest set of communities and exposes an API and MCP so an agent can read the feed. F5Bot is the free option for Reddit, Hacker News and Lobsters; check its terms before commercial use. For app products add competitor app-review mining.
slots.details: Pick changed from F5Bot to Syften on capability; F5Bot now best_free. GummySearch is shut down.

verify.note: Prices confirmed on official page. Best overall holds: widest sources, AI filtering, API/MCP; GummySearch is dead.

pick.name: ChatGPT deep research
pick.what: OpenAI agentic research reports
pick.why: Mature, strong at long structured reports.
pick.free_limits: Free plan: 'limited deep research'; Plus 'expanded'; Pro 'maximum'. Exact counts are shown only in an in-product counter and reset every 30 days for fixed monthly allowances. Availability varies by country. Reports export to Markdown, Word and PDF

best_free.name: Gemini Deep Research (free tier)
best_free.what: Agentic cited research reports grounded in Google Search, exportable to Docs
best_free.why: Free Gemini accounts can run limited Deep Research; Perplexity free is the fast-answer fallback.
best_free.free_limits: Deep Research is available without a Google AI plan under standard compute-based limits that refresh every 5 hours up to a weekly cap (Deep Research is a high-cost feature). Google AI Plus 2x, Pro 4x, Ultra 5x or 20x the Pro limit. Free context window 32k tokens

alts.name: Claude Research
alts.what: Multi-step web plus connector research with citations (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise)
alts.why: Strong reasoning over messy sources and reads connected tools (Gmail, Calendar, Docs and other connectors) during research.
alts.free_limits: No free plan: Research is available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise (web, desktop, mobile; mobile searches the web only). Same limits as normal chats but uses them faster

alts.name: Perplexity
alts.what: Fast cited search plus Deep Research mode
alts.why: Best for quick sourced answers; less depth on long reports.
alts.free_limits: Free tier with limited Pro searches; deep research listed as a Pro feature. Pro was on a limited-time 50% discount ($9/mo billed annually) at check time. Consumer Pro/Max are marked 'for personal use only'; business use is on Enterprise plans

candidates.name: Gemini Deep Research
candidates.verdict: best_free route; grounded in Google Search

slots.decision: The major deep-research products are close in quality. Claude Research reasons well over many sources and can read connected Google Workspace and other connectors, but it has no free tier. ChatGPT deep research is the strongest alternative: an editable research plan, restriction to chosen sites, Word/PDF/Markdown export and a limited free allowance. Gemini Deep Research is the free route. Run market sizing through two vendors and reconcile, since disagreement shows where a TAM number is soft.
slots.details: Gemini limits moved to compute-based multipliers around May 2026.

verify.note: The original decision justified the pick by 'consistent with its Claude Code stance'. BRIEF limits the Claude stance to the coding agent and Claude Code ecosystem slots, so that reasoning is removed. Not a clear wrong_pick, but the editor should consider ChatGPT deep research as pick.

better.name: ChatGPT deep research
better.reason: Comparable quality plus editable research plans, site restriction, Word/PDF export and a limited free tier (Plus 'expanded', Pro 'maximum'); arguably the better default for a neutral founder audience.

pick.name: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)
pick.what: Upload sources and get cited answers, audio/video overviews, reports
pick.why: Purpose-built source-grounded workspace with a usable free tier; nothing else matches its audio/video overviews.
pick.free_limits: Free (Standard): 100 notebooks, 50 sources per notebook; Plus 200/100; Pro 500/300; Ultra 500/500-600. Visible watermark on generated outputs: removal only on Google AI Pro/Ultra, and never for users residing in India, South Korea or Vietnam

best_free.name: Obsidian + Claude Code (local vault)
best_free.what: Local markdown vault that Claude Code can read and grep
best_free.why: Free for commercial use, fully local, no lock-in; the choice for confidential material.
best_free.free_limits: Free incl. commercial use; optional paid sync/publish

alts.name: Claude Projects
alts.what: Project knowledge plus chat over uploaded files
alts.why: Better reasoning and writing over the same pack; no audio overviews.
alts.free_limits: Within plan limits; free-plan availability unverified

alts.name: Perplexity Spaces
alts.what: Collections with files and web search
alts.why: Good when you want web plus your files together.
alts.free_limits: Consumer plans are marked 'for personal use only'; business use via Enterprise

slots.decision: NotebookLM is the best source-grounded notebook for a general founder and has a free tier. Use a local vault plus Claude Code when sources are client-confidential or regulated.
slots.details: Google's help page may call it 'Gemini Notebook'; rename unconfirmed.

region_notes.India: Outputs from Gemini Notebook carry a visible watermark for residents of India on every plan (also South Korea and Vietnam).

pick.name: Distill.io (free)
pick.what: Page-change monitor (cloud + local browser-extension monitors)
pick.why: No server to run or keep online, and 25 free monitors (5 cloud) cover a typical solo founder's competitor set.
pick.free_limits: Free: 25 monitors (5 cloud), 1,000 cloud checks/mo, min interval 6 h, 30 email alerts/mo. Starter $15/mo

best_free.name: changedetection.io
best_free.what: Open-source page-change monitor, self-host or hosted
best_free.why: Unlimited monitors for anyone willing to run a small always-on server or container (free, Apache-2.0); hosted version $8.99/mo.
best_free.free_limits: Self-host free (Apache-2.0); hosted $8.99/mo per README

alts.name: Visualping (free)
alts.why: Faster interval on free (60 min) but only 5 pages and free is marketed to individuals.

alts.name: Wappalyzer
alts.what: Detects the tech stack of any site
alts.why: Complements change monitoring with stack lookups.

slots.decision: Distill needs no server and covers a solo founder competitor set free. Self-host changedetection.io (Apache-2.0) for unlimited monitors and webhooks; Visualping if you want visual diffs.

slots.decision: Ollama is the default runner for development and sidecar use on any OS; drop to llama.cpp for bleeding-edge models and tuning, MLX LM on Apple silicon for speed, vLLM for multi-user GPU serving. Local models trade quality for privacy and zero marginal cost.
slots.details: GPU support per docs.ollama.com/gpu: NVIDIA compute capability 5.0+ (driver 550+), AMD Radeon via ROCm v7 (Linux broad; Windows select RX 7000/PRO W7000), Apple Metal, and Vulkan on Windows/Linux.

os_notes.macOS: Apple silicon uses unified memory: 16GB runs 4-8B Q4 comfortably, 32GB+ runs 20-30B MoE; MLX LM is the fastest path.
os_notes.Windows: Native installer; NVIDIA GPUs (driver 550+) and select AMD RX 7000/PRO W7000 GPUs used automatically, Vulkan covers other GPUs, otherwise CPU. WSL not needed.
os_notes.Linux: NVIDIA (CUDA, compute capability 5.0+), AMD Radeon/Instinct via ROCm v7, or Vulkan; vLLM for multi-user server throughput.

slots.decision: A merchant of record (MoR) is the legal seller to your customers and handles VAT, sales tax, fraud and chargebacks, the lowest-effort path for a small team selling software globally. Paddle is the best overall: the longest-established software MoR, one all-in rate (5% + 50c) with no international-card surcharge listed, and credible with enterprise buyers. Choose Polar for developer experience and open source (cheaper than Paddle only on its paid Pro/Growth tiers at volume), and Stripe direct when you need full control, marketplaces or services billing and can handle tax registration.
slots.details: Dodo payout-fee pages conflict (Free vs $5 under $1,000): unverified. No free option is recommended for this job.

region_notes.India: Stripe is invite-only for Indian businesses and India is not a Managed Payments business location; Paddle, Polar or Dodo (which also takes INR cards/UPI and pays out to Indian banks) are the practical routes, with Razorpay or Cashfree for domestic INR/UPI customers.
region_notes.US: MoRs remove sales-tax nexus tracking for the products they sell; you still handle your own income tax. Verify with a professional.
region_notes.EU: The MoR is the supplier of record, so you do not register for EU VAT (or the non-Union OSS) on sales it makes; the MoR pays you net. Verify with a professional.
region_notes.UK: The MoR accounts for UK VAT on its sales, so an overseas seller avoids UK VAT registration for those sales (GOV.UK: when a platform is responsible, it accounts for the VAT). Verify with a professional.

verify.note: Stress-tested vs Polar, Lemon Squeezy, Dodo: Paddle 5% + 50c, no monthly fee, tax filing/remittance, chargebacks and fraud included, no separate international-card surcharge listed. Polar Starter is the same 5% + 50c PLUS 1.5% on non-US cards, $15/dispute and Stripe payout fees ($2/mo active + 0.25% + 25c per payout + 0.25-1% FX), so Paddle is cheaper for global sales until Polar Pro/Growth tiers ($20-100/mo, 3.8%/3.6%) pay off at higher volume. Dodo 4% + 40c base but +1.5% non-US, +0.5% subscriptions, and its payout fee is contradictory (table 'Free' vs FAQ '$5 if payout < $1,000'). Lemon Squeezy is in transition to Stripe Managed Payments (Jan 2026 post: slower support, fewer updates) and should not be recommended for new builds. Paddle stays.

slots.decision: For a solo founder, a merchant of record is the simplest way to stay compliant globally. Add Stripe Tax or a specialist like Anrok only if you must remain seller of record (enterprise contracts, marketplaces, margins). Verify with a professional.
slots.details: Merged: the India GST and income-tax slots fold into this global slot plus region_notes. Sources: EU OSS (europa.eu Your Europe + vat-one-stop-shop.ec.europa.eu), GOV.UK digital-services VAT guidance, GST portal LUT tutorial, RBI/FEMA 2026 export regulations (EY alert). Tax content: verify with a professional. No free option is recommended for this job.

region_notes.US: Since South Dakota v. Wayfair (2018) each state sets its own economic-nexus threshold, most commonly USD 100,000 of sales into the state (some add a transaction count, several removed the 200-transaction test in 2025-26; Alabama uses USD 250,000). Whether SaaS is taxable also varies by state. A MoR or Stripe Tax tracks this. Verify with a professional.
region_notes.EU: Non-EU businesses selling services to EU consumers charge VAT at the customer's member-state rate from the first euro (the EUR 10,000 threshold applies only to EU-established sellers). The non-Union OSS lets them register in one member state and file one quarterly return; B2B sales to VAT-registered EU businesses are generally reverse-charged. A MoR removes this for the sales it makes. Verify with a professional.
region_notes.UK: A business based outside the UK that supplies digital services to UK consumers must register for UK VAT, with no threshold (GOV.UK); if a platform or MoR makes the sale, the platform accounts for the VAT. Verify with HMRC guidance or an adviser.
region_notes.India: GST registration is required above Rs 20 lakh aggregate turnover (Rs 10 lakh in special-category states), and exports count toward it. Zero-rated export of services without paying IGST needs a Letter of Undertaking (Form GST RFD-11) filed each financial year before exporting, and payment in convertible foreign exchange evidenced by an e-FIRC/e-BRC. Under FEMA's 2026 export regulations (in force 1 Oct 2026) export proceeds must be realised within 9 months (previously 15). Whether sales routed through a foreign MoR qualify as export of services needs CA advice.

verify.note: Region notes rewritten against official sources (EU OSS portal / Your Europe, GOV.UK, GST portal) plus current RBI rules. Note the India realisation period changed in 2026.
